methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents intentional capacity-building in a traditionally non-hub region, potentially distributing deep AI fluency beyond metro corridors if it achieves sustainable peer network effects beyond the initial institutional launch.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting the 'technology gap' in Hampton Roads signal grassroots distribution efforts, though success depends on whether participants develop deep capability or remain in shallow tool-use—the Norfolk native's approach suggests peer-driven depth over platform dependency.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU partnering with AI Ready RVA concentrates institutional resources and innovation capacity in Richmond's metro core, deepening the capital region's AI ecosystem while the 'community impact' framing reveals awareness that benefits may not automatically distribute to surrounding areas.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M data center investment adding 200 jobs in Henrico signals infrastructure concentration rather than capability distribution—these facilities power AI elsewhere while creating local operations jobs that require shallow rather than deep AI fluency.

signals.title: Richmond summer program helps visually impaired students explore careers in technology and cybersecurity - WTVR.com
signals.signal_reading: Targeting visually impaired students for technology and cybersecurity careers demonstrates intentional equity-focused skill-building that could deepen AI capability in underrepresented groups, though its Richmond location and summer program format may limit geographic distribution.
